summary: Replaced the B445/B455 iframe-embedded HTTP dashboard extension with a native VS Code Webview application. extension.js now owns exactly one bounded repo-local `python3 -m geoai_task_mcp.server` stdio child and a hand-rolled JSON-RPC 2.0 ClientSession (initialize -> notifications/initialized -> tools/call), with exact monotonically-increasing request ids, a bounded pending-request map (MCP_MAX_PENDING_REQUESTS=16) with a per-request timeout (MCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS=20s), a response-size cap on unterminated stdout (MCP_MAX_LINE_BYTES=8MiB), sanitized/redacted stderr logging, and exactly one bounded restart attempt (MCP_MAX_RESTART_ATTEMPTS=1) on unexpected child exit. Added tools/geoai-task-mcp/src/geoai_task_mcp/dashboard_mcp_app.py: three narrow read-only MCP tools (geoai_dashboard_snapshot, geoai_dashboard_task_detail, geoai_dashboard_health) that call ONLY dashboard.build_snapshot()/build_task_detail()/core.health() -- the same canonical builders the pre-existing HTTP dashboard's /api/snapshot and /api/task routes already use -- with a defensive transport-size bound (never a data-model change) and dashboard._TASK_ID_RE task_id validation reused as-is (no second regex). Wired via dashboard_mcp_app.register(mcp) in server.py, mirroring the existing cli_adapter_readonly_tool.register(mcp) pattern. The Webview (media/app.js + media/app.css) is a from-scratch native rewrite of the old dashboard.js/dashboard.css: no fetch/XHR, no iframe, no window.prompt/confirm, no archive/restore (read-only only); it sends only a fixed message enum (ready/refresh/retry/selectTask/setAutoRefresh/setRefreshInterval) validated against an allowlist plus a bounded task_id regex, and receives only snapshot/taskDetail/offline/error messages back from the extension host -- it never receives a coordinator token, env value, filesystem path, MCP capability, child-process handle, or arbitrary tool-call primitive. CSP is a strict per-render nonce (`script-src 'nonce-<random>'`, `frame-src 'none'`, no unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval, only webview.cspSource for style/img/font). All dynamic content is textContent/DOM construction (createElement/replaceChildren); innerHTML is never assigned. The one retained full-editor WebviewPanel is created once and reused via panel.reveal(); both it and the Activity Bar WebviewView get a host-owned ViewState whose setInterval poll timer is cleared by onDidChangeVisibility/onDidChangeViewState the instant a view is hidden and only rescheduled while visible -- polling-stop is a host-side fact, not a hope that a backgrounded script pauses itself. Remote-SSH needs no owner-managed forwarding: extensionKind stays ["workspace"] so the MCP child is colocated with the extension host already; there is no HTTP listener, no vscode.env.asExternalUri call, and no tunnel anywhere in the new code path. package.json dropped dashboardUrl/autoStart in favor of one refreshIntervalMs setting (10000/30000/60000, default 30000); the three commands (openDashboard/refreshDashboard/restartDashboard, the last retitled 'Restart Task MCP Connection') and the Activity Bar container/WebviewView id are preserved unchanged. install_remote.sh needed no functional change (it already copies media/ recursively); only a stale 'autoStart' comment was corrected. This first native MCP App stays strictly read-only end to end: the write gate (GEOAI_TASK_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES) and launch gate (GEOAI_TASK_MCP_ALLOW_LAUNCH) are explicitly deleted from the spawned child's environment regardless of the ambient extension-host environment, and no archive/restore/done/reject/launch affordance exists anywhere in the Webview or extension host; the pre-existing Task MCP workers/callback bridge/HTTP dashboard server are unchanged and continue operating independently.

architecture_change.before: extension.js ran a bounded /healthz + autostart loop against a loopback HTTP dashboard process, then framed the dashboard's own served HTML in a sandboxed <iframe> resolved through vscode.env.asExternalUri against an explicit /embed/vscode CSP-relaxed route.
architecture_change.after: extension.js spawns and owns exactly one `python3 -m geoai_task_mcp.server` stdio child, drives it with a hand-rolled JSON-RPC 2.0 client (no npm dependency), and renders a fully native Webview (media/app.js + media/app.css) built from the MCP tool responses -- no HTTP server, no iframe, no asExternalUri, no LAN IP, no manual port forwarding anywhere in the path.

mcp_stdio_client.request_id_scheme: monotonic integer, exact per-request, never reused
mcp_stdio_client.stderr_handling: bounded length + redaction of 24+ char opaque token-shaped substrings before logging
mcp_stdio_client.restart_policy: exactly one bounded restart attempt on unexpected child exit, then native offline/retry state
mcp_stdio_client.write_gate_env: GEOAI_TASK_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES deleted from child env before spawn
mcp_stdio_client.launch_gate_env: GEOAI_TASK_MCP_ALLOW_LAUNCH deleted from child env before spawn

dashboard_mcp_tools.task_id_validation: reuses dashboard._TASK_ID_RE (same compiled pattern object) -- no second regex
dashboard_mcp_tools.server_wiring: dashboard_mcp_app.register(mcp) called from server.py, same pattern as cli_adapter_readonly_tool.register(mcp)

extension_call_sites.geoai_dashboard_snapshot: pushSnapshot() -- called on ready/refresh/retry and by each view's poll timer
extension_call_sites.geoai_dashboard_task_detail: pushTaskDetail() -- called on selectTask with a regex-validated task_id
extension_call_sites.geoai_dashboard_health: restartMcpConnectionCommand() -- confirms the freshly (re)started session actually answers, distinct from the full snapshot pull

rendering.panel_reuse: single createWebviewPanel call, reveal() on subsequent opens, retainContextWhenHidden true

remote_ssh.offline_diagnostic: native offline/retry banner posted to the Webview on no_workspace_folder / spawn failure / handshake timeout / restart exhaustion -- never a browser

Verified instead via `python3 -m py_compile` on dashboard_mcp_app.py, server.py, and test_dashboard_mcp_app.py (all compile cleanly) and by manual trace of every test against the implementation. The coordinator is expected to re-run this exact pytest command in an environment with `pytest`/`mcp` installed as part of its independent validation rerun.
